svg.text: One press fixes distance and aim, anywhere on the arc
Seen from above, red audience cell. You choose where on the arc to stop; the button only turns in place and drives forward or in reverse.
AUDIENCE WALL (your drivers stand here)
RED SIDE WALL
UP CELL
bottom lip
the arc
BACK (shooters)
PRIMARY
teach here once
FRONT (intake)
LEFT: 40 degrees around
Dashed outline: the driver stopped 120 mm
too far from the cell and 10 degrees off.
One press: the robot turns to aim, then
reverses 120 mm toward the cell along its
aim line. Its back now aims 63 mm left of
the lip's middle.
RIGHT: 38 degrees around
The mirror image: the back aims 59 mm
right of the lip's middle. The button
never slides the robot along the arc;
where you stop on the arc is the driver's
choice.
What you see
Long dashes = the arc. Every point on it is the
same distance from the aim point (ringed cross,
the middle of the cell floor) as the primary is.
The robots
Grey square = the robot after one press. Dashed
outline = where the driver stopped. Thick black
edge = the robot's back, where the shooters are.
The front (intake) faces away from the cell.
The aim
Short dashes = where the robot's back points.
Black dot = where that line crosses the bottom
lip. Robot 457 x 457 mm. One tile = 610 mm.
